To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the selectivity measures that are most commonly used to characterize object detectors (precision, CCMAS, and network dissection) provide misleadingly high estimates of selectivity and (2) the units that are most selective are poor object detectors.

(1) the different measures of selectivity provide different estimates of selectivity and (2) units that are selective for a given class according to one measure are often not selective for that class according to other measures
(a) CNNs trained on ImageNet do not learn selective object representations, and (b) units in these networks are poor at object classification
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how selective are the units in CNNs trained on natural scenes, and the answer seems to be 'not very'.
the nature of object selectivity in the hidden units of convolutional neural networks (CNNs).
how well CNNs can detect objects and what the functional relevance of object selectivity is in these networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hidden layers of convolutional neural networks are not 'object detectors', and that object representations are not learned in the early layers of the visual hierarchy.
there are no object detectors in the hidden layers in CNNs trained on natural image datasets.
there is no evidence of any 'object detectors'.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the object representations in CNNs are not selective enough to be used for object recognition, and that the 'object detectors' reported in the literature are not selective enough for object detection.
there are no object detectors in the hidden layers, and the units are not selective enough to be used for classification.
there are no object detectors in CNNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the units in CNNs trained to classify images of objects and scenes are not object detectors.
object detectors do not exist in CNNs, and that the object detectors that have been described in the literature are not object detectors.
